messages:
Samir: FYI found a repeatable weirdo when prefix demote + eviction happen during a long-running read. Read sees value A, then evict+rehydrate returns stale A even though writer wrote B.
Priya: ouch. repro steps?
Samir: Quick steps: 1) pin prefix, 2) long cursor reading seq 100..200, 3) concurrent write updates prefix to B & commits, 4) demote triggers eviction, prefill path wins but uses old KV snapshot.
Samir: Minimal log snippet:
``nread cursor start=100
write commit seq=150 -> value=B
evict prefix id=0xabc demote -> prefill started
prefill applied snapshot.seq=120 -> populated cache with A
read continues -> returns A
```
Priya: hmm looks like prefill is allowed to use an older snapshot than the write commit. Could be lease/fence ordering bug.
Alex: Did we observe the prefix handshake/lease bump? If the demote lets a prefill task read from a slightly older epoch we can end up regressing.
Marta: This smells like: prefill reads from storage without verifying latest residency token before install. We should compare snapshot.seq with latest lease epoch or generation.
Samir: Right. I can repro on dev with small harness. I'll attach a trace.
Samir: Repro steps attached (inline): run long-reader.sh + spawn writer at t+2s + trigger demote at t+3s.
eng-bot: CI: prefills test failed on canary-evict branch (build 482). Link: https://ci.redwood/482/logs
Jamie: Quick mitigation: make prefill install conditional - only install if storage snapshot.seq >= current_prefix_gen OR if lease==held_by_us. Otherwise drop prefill and let reader miss/cache-miss and go to storage directly.
Priya: tradeoffs: dropping prefill increases latency for cold reads but keeps correctness. We could also make prefill read at a guaranteed barrier (block until commit epoch advances) but that hurts throughput.
Alex: Another option: install prefill but mark it 'tentative' with an attached generation token; readers must check generation on read and if mismatch, re-read from storage or wait for rehydrate. Cheaper than blocking prefill.
Marta: Tentative installs sound promising. Implementation sketch: store meta {gen: X, tentative: true}. On read if gen!=current_gen -> kick async repair and return miss. Also emit metric "prefill_tentative_mismatch" so we can gauge fallout.
Samir: I like tentative + metric. Easier rollout. What about long-lived cursors that assume stable snapshot? If tentative get returned mid-cursor we might break cursor semantics.
Jamie: For cursors we can special-case: if cursor was started before tentative install, keep returning from the cursor's snapshot until it finishes. Only new cursors see tentative semantics. That keeps read-after-start semantics intact.
Priya: Need to be careful with multi-tenant shared cache: tentative markers add complexity for eviction ordering. Might increase memory retention if we hold both tentative and final entries.
Alex: Eviction policy tweak: treat tentative entries as low-priority for eviction. If we later materialize final entry, overwrite and clear tentative. If prefill fails to become final within Xs, evict it.
Marta: Also add safety check: when applying prefill we should fetch prefix generation token atomically with the storage read (or use read-with-generation RPC). If read's gen < observed commit gen, mark tentative false; else tentative true.
Samir: Action items: 1) I'll open a small PR with tentative flag + metric + reader check (opt-in behind feature flag). 2) Priya, can you run canary with 10% traffic? 3) Jamie, add cursor-start-gen metadata to cursor allocator.
Priya: Ack. I'll schedule canary test after PR.
Alex: Also add test harness: concurrent read/writer/demote scenario to e2e prefills. Repro is reliable so we should gate.
Samir: Thanks. I'll post the trace + minimal failing unit in the PR description.
Marta: One more thought: log an alert if tentative mismatch rate > 0.1% of reads for a tenant in 5m window. Could indicate storage snapshots lagging commit path.
eng-bot: Jira issue created: INF-2142 "prefill tentative install to avoid stale-install regressions" assigned to Samir.
Jamie: Nice. if we converge on tentative semantics we should update docs for prefix-ownership guarantees.
Samir: agreed. I'll draft a short note in the arch repo once PR lands. :+1:
